McDonald's pulls $3.96 million per store. Burger King does $1.63 million. Same street, different planet. 2.4 times the revenue from the same real estate. That gap is the whole story. Getting in costs $1.47 million with McDonald's. Burger King lets you start at $232K. 6.3 times cheaper to open the doors. That's the difference between dream and bank loan. McDonald's cheeseburger runs $1.91 an ounce and still ranks. Burger King doesn't even chart. McDonald's takes it 3 to 2. Pick Burger King only if capital is your ceiling.
uploads.youtubeTitle: McDonald's vs Burger King: The Revenue Gap Nobody Talks About
uploads.youtubeDescription:
McDonald's averages $3.96 million per location against Burger King's $1.63 million, a 2.4x gap on the same kind of corner lot. But getting into McDonald's costs $1.47 million versus $232K for Burger King. We break down revenue per store, entry cost and menu pricing to name a winner.

uploads.title: Ww1 vs Ww2
uploads.transcript: One war killed 20 million. The sequel killed up to 85. Same continent, twenty years apart. The difference is who ended up dying. Roughly 20 million against 70 to 85 million. The sequel quadrupled the bill. Seven million civilians versus up to 55 million. That gap is the whole story. Under 40 percent civilian in one war, up to 65 in the other. Killing moved off the battlefield. One of these wars never touched the Pacific. The other lost 25 million there. China and Japan alone cost more lives than the entire First World War. On every count, WW1 was the smaller catastrophe. Study WW2 to see war go total.
uploads.youtubeTitle: WW1 vs WW2: The Death Tolls Compared
uploads.youtubeDescription:
A stat by stat comparison of World War 1 and World War 2, covering total deaths, civilian casualties, the civilian share of the dead, and the Pacific and China-Japan theatres. WW1 killed around 20 million. WW2 killed 70 to 85 million, most of them civilians.
